intervention_names: Drug: Henagliflozin Proline,Retagliptin Phosphate and Metformin Hydrochloride Sustained-release Tablets
arm_groups.label: Fixed-dose combination of henagliflozin, retagliptin and metformin ER

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the fixed-dose combination of henagliflozin, retagliptin and metformin extended-release can improve glycemic control and achieve clinical remission in adults with short-duration type 2 diabetes mellitus.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the fixed-dose combination regimen improve Time In Target Range (TITR) compared with sequential metformin monotherapy? Does the fixed-dose combination regimen increase the rate of clinical remission of type 2 diabetes mellitus?

Researchers will compare the fixed-dose combination of henagliflozin, retagliptin and metformin extended-release versus sequential metformin extended-release monotherapy to see if the fixed-dose combination provides superior benefits on glycemic control and clinical remission.

Participants will:

* Receive study treatment assigned by randomization
* Undergo regular clinic visits, laboratory tests and continuous glucose monitoring assessments during the study period
* Complete follow-up evaluations according to the study schedule
brief_title: Fixed-Dose Combination of Henagliflozin Proline,Retagliptin Phosphate and Metformin Hydrochloride Sustained-release Tablets Versus Sequential Metformin Monotherapy in Type 2 Diabetes

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Aged 18-65 years, of either sex.
2. Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus, disease duration ≤ 2 years.
3. HbA1c 7.5% - 9.5% at screening.
4. Only received lifestyle intervention, or prior metformin / DPP-4 inhibitor monotherapy, without prior use of SGLT-2 inhibitors.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. History of diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic coma.
3. Known allergy to henagliflozin, retagliptin, metformin or any excipients of the study drugs.
4. Pregnant, breastfeeding or women of childbearing potential who refuse effective contraception.
5. Participation in other interventional clinical trials within 3 months before screening.
6. Any other conditions that the investigator considers inappropriate for enrollment.
